Sunset Riding: The Golden Hour Guide

There is no finer moment on a motorcycle tour than riding into a sunset. The golden light transforms the landscape, the temperature softens, and the road ahead glows amber. Britain's west-facing coastlines and hilltop roads offer some extraordinary sunset riding opportunities. Here are the best.

West Coast Scotland

Scotland's west coast faces the Atlantic, and in summer the sun sets dramatically over the Hebrides and open ocean. The best spots include:

  • Applecross Bay: After descending the Bealach na Bà, the village of Applecross faces west across to Skye. Sunset here is stunning — the sky turns pink and gold above the island silhouettes.
  • Arisaig to Mallaig road: The A830 along the Silver Sands of Morar faces due west. On a clear evening, the sunset over the Small Isles (Eigg, Rum, Muck) is breathtaking.
  • Durness: On the north coast, sunset in midsummer happens around 10:30pm, and the sky stays light until midnight. Sango Sands beach below Durness offers a theatrical setting.

Cornwall and Devon

England's southwest peninsula catches spectacular sunsets year-round:

  • Sennen Cove, near Land's End: The last sunset stop in England. The beach faces due west and the sun drops into the Atlantic.
  • Hartland Point, North Devon: A remote headland with views across to Lundy Island. The coastal road is narrow and quiet — perfect for a sunset ride.
  • St Agnes Head, Cornwall: Former mining landscape silhouetted against a sunset. The engine houses create iconic shapes against the sky.

Wales

  • Rhossili Bay, Gower: Regularly voted one of Britain's best beaches, Rhossili faces west and the sunset over Worms Head is legendary. The road down to the bay is a pleasant ride.
  • Aberystwyth promenade: The Victorian promenade faces due west across Cardigan Bay. Ride along the seafront as the sun goes down.
  • South Stack, Anglesey: The lighthouse at the western tip of Anglesey catches spectacular sunsets, especially in spring and autumn when the sun sets over the Irish Sea.

England's Hilltop Sunsets

  • Hartside Summit, A686: At 1,904ft, the western view catches sunsets over the Eden Valley and the Lake District fells beyond. The café is gone but the viewpoint remains.
  • Sutton Bank, North York Moors: The western escarpment faces across the Vale of York. On clear evenings, the sunset spreads across the entire horizon.
Sunset riding means dusk riding — ensure your visor is clean, your headlight works, and you have a clear visor for the ride home in fading light. The golden hour is magical but transitions quickly into the dangerous half-light of twilight.

Timing Tips

  • Golden hour begins approximately one hour before sunset. Plan to arrive at your viewpoint by this time.
  • UK midsummer sunsets: 9-10:30pm (further north = later). Plan a late afternoon ride to catch it.
  • UK midwinter sunsets: 3:30-4:30pm. Useful for short afternoon rides ending with golden light.
  • Clear skies produce clean sunsets, but scattered cloud creates the most dramatic colours.
  • Check sunset times for your location at timeanddate.com

A sunset stop is the perfect end to a touring day. Park up, remove your helmet, and watch the world turn gold. These moments are what motorcycle touring memories are made of.

Geology for Riders

The Jurassic Coast tells 185 million years of Earth's history in 95 miles of coastline. As you ride east, you travel forward through geological time — from the ancient Triassic deserts at Exmouth to the Jurassic seas at Lyme Regis and the Cretaceous chalk at Studland. The rock colours change from red to grey to white as you ride, and the landscape transforms accordingly.

Fossil hunting at Lyme Regis and Charmouth is a fantastic off-bike activity. Ammonites and belemnites wash out of the cliffs regularly, and you can find them by simply walking along the beach after a storm. Guided fossil walks are available and reveal the area's extraordinary history.

The coastal villages along the route — West Bay, Burton Bradstock, Abbotsbury, and Worth Matravers — each have excellent pubs and cafes. Plan your riding around lunch stops and you'll discover that the Jurassic Coast is as rewarding for gastronomy as it is for geology and scenery.

Surfing Heritage and Beach Culture

Cornwall's north coast is Britain's surfing heartland. Fistral Beach in Newquay, Polzeath, and Bude all have vibrant surf cultures. Even if you don't surf, the beach cafes and laid-back atmosphere make excellent stops between riding sections. A flat white and a view of Atlantic breakers is a fine way to break up a touring day.

The south coast has a different character — sheltered harbours, subtropical gardens, and the glamour of Falmouth and St Mawes. The Helford River, navigable by passenger ferry, runs through ancient woodland to the sea. The roads around the Helford are narrow and canopied — completely different from the exposed north coast.

Cornish pasties are the touring rider's perfect food — self-contained, hot, portable, and delicious. Every village bakery makes their own, and local opinion on the best pasty is fiercely held. Ann's Pasties in The Lizard and Philps in Hayle are consistently excellent.

Dark Skies and Stargazing

Northumberland contains the largest area of International Dark Sky Park in Europe. Kielder Forest and the surrounding areas have virtually zero light pollution, making this one of the best stargazing locations in the Northern Hemisphere. Combine a day's riding with an evening of stargazing for a unique touring experience.

The Northumberland coast is also rich in wildlife. The Farne Islands, visible from the shore, host one of the UK's largest seabird colonies — puffins, guillemots, razorbills, and Arctic terns nest here from May to July. Boat trips from Seahouses take you within metres of the nesting birds.

Alnwick is worth a longer stop. Beyond the famous castle (used as Hogwarts in the Harry Potter films) and the Alnwick Garden, the town has excellent independent bookshops, including the famous Barter Books — one of the largest secondhand bookshops in Europe, housed in the former railway station.

Island Excursions

Pembrokeshire's offshore islands add a unique dimension to a touring visit. Boat trips to Skomer Island run daily in summer from Martin's Haven — the island is home to thousands of puffins, Manx shearwaters, and grey seals. It's a short ride from the coast road to the departure point.

Ramsey Island, off St David's Head, offers wildlife boat trips that circle the island, passing through tide races where porpoises and dolphins are regularly spotted. The dramatic sea cliffs and caves of Ramsey are visible from the coast road but far more impressive from the water.

Caldey Island, off Tenby, is home to a Cistercian monastery where monks make perfume and chocolate. The short ferry crossing from Tenby harbour gives a peaceful contrast to the riding roads. The combination of motorcycling and island hopping makes Pembrokeshire unique among Welsh touring destinations.
keyTakeaways: West-facing coasts deliver the best sunsets, especially Scotland's Atlantic seaboard over the Hebrides.
Applecross Bay, the Arisaig to Mallaig A830, and Sennen Cove near Land's End are standout stops.
Rhossili Bay on the Gower and South Stack on Anglesey are Wales's finest sunset viewpoints.
Midsummer UK sunsets fall between 9pm and 10:30pm, later the further north you ride.
Sunset means dusk riding, so carry a clean clear visor and ensure your headlight works for the ride home.

comparisonTable.caption: Where to catch the best sunsets by bike

faq.q: What time do sunsets happen across the UK through the year?
faq.a: In midsummer the sun sets between roughly 9pm and 10:30pm, later the further north you go, so a late afternoon ride catches it. Around the equinoxes sunset is early evening, and in midwinter it drops to 3:30 to 4:30pm, which suits a short afternoon ride finishing in golden light. Check exact times for your location before setting out.

faq.q: How do I plan a safe ride home after sunset?
faq.a: Golden hour is beautiful but transitions quickly into low-light twilight, when glare and poor contrast make riding harder. Fit or carry a clean clear visor rather than a tinted one, check your headlight and rear light before you leave, and add reflective elements to your gear. Plan a route home on familiar roads and ride at a pace matched to your visibility.

faq.q: Which coast is best for sunset riding?
faq.a: Any west-facing coast works, but Scotland's Atlantic seaboard is exceptional. Applecross faces Skye, and the A830 along the Silver Sands of Morar looks out to the Small Isles of Eigg, Rum, and Muck. In summer the far north around Durness stays light until near midnight. Cornwall's Sennen Cove and Wales's Rhossili Bay are outstanding southern alternatives.

faq.q: Does clear weather guarantee the best sunset?
faq.a: Not necessarily. A completely clear sky produces a clean but sometimes plain sunset, whereas scattered cloud catches and scatters the light into far more dramatic colour. Aim to arrive at your chosen viewpoint about an hour before sunset, when golden hour begins, so you have time to park safely, settle, and photograph the changing sky.
